gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, with curve endings that keep their distance from each other. Origami, in single-stroke brush weight, sits above it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo reads with a sizable x-height and curved letters whose mouths stay wide open on the screen. Origami, with every stroke the same gauge, earns its keep when it runs big and short.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-sundanes: Clean and unfussy, Noto Sans Sundanese gives its e crossbars open mouths and keeps x-height close to cap height. Origami adds neon-tube letters glowing with one line thickness, and that glow is the pair's boldest quality.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Noto Sans Sunuwar leaves daylight in its curves like a rope's open bight, with short ascender stems on tall lowercase bodies. Noto Sans Sunuwar goes down smoothly over a long stretch, while Origami's bold, uniform strokes stay up top.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: Chunky, brushed and sign-painted, Origami gives its y a tail as thick as its arm, while Noto Sans Syloti Nagri keeps short ascenders and a tall x-height. Origami's single stroke is the hook.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac reads warmly, its tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs and its s shapes taking wide, easy turns. Origami, true monoline throughout, brings a single drawn line over the top of it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-syriac-e: Origami looks drawn by a fixed-width nib, a lowercase mass like poured lead type with one unvarying stroke. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern follows with tall lowercase against small caps, easy going over a full page.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-syriac-w: Origami looks drawn with a compass pencil. Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke body, and shrinking the heading would squeeze that consistency, while a large body would lose its bundled-cable density.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Origami swaps thin hairline joins for full-width stroke connections. Noto Sans Tagalog lets the middle zone dominate each line, with generous gaps in the curves, so a long stretch of text reads with a steady, open texture.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Origami has a ballpoint's pressure-free line weight, a single brush stroke at constant width, with a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Noto Sans Tagbanwa fills most of the height with open curves, so it reads easily over a long passage.
